verses.text: A man named Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold a piece of property.
He secretly kept some of the money back. His wife knew about it. He brought only part of the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
Peter said, “Ananias, why did you let Satan fill your heart and lie to the Holy Spirit by holding back some of the money from the land?
Before you sold it, wasn’t it yours? And after you sold it, wasn’t the money yours to do with as you wanted? Why hatch this plan in your heart? You didn’t lie to people—you lied to God.”
When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. Everyone who heard about it was shaken with fear.
Some young men got up, wrapped his body, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter asked her, “Tell me, is this the amount you got for the land?” She said, “Yes, that’s the amount.”
Peter said to her, “How did you two agree to test the Spirit of the Lord? Listen—the feet of the people who buried your husband are at the door, and they’ll carry you out too.”
She fell down at once at his feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear swept through the whole church and everyone who heard about these events.
Many signs and wonders kept happening among the people through the apostles. They all met together in Solomon’s Colonnade.
The rest didn’t dare join them, but the people held them in high regard.
More and more believers were added to the Lord—crowds of both men and women.
People even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and mats, hoping that as Peter passed by, his shadow might fall on some of them.
Crowds also came from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing sick people and those tormented by unclean spirits. They were all healed.
The high priest and all his allies—the Sadducees—stood up, burning with jealousy.
They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
But during the night, an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors, led them out, and said,
Go to the temple and tell the people the whole message about this life.
They heard him and went into the temple at daybreak to teach. Meanwhile, the high priest and his allies called the council together—the full senate of Israel—and sent for the apostles from the jail.
But when the officers got there, they didn’t find them in the prison. They went back and reported,
“We found the prison locked tight and the guards standing at the doors. But when we opened up, there was nobody inside!”
When the captain of the temple guard, the chief priests, and the high priest heard this, they were baffled and wondered what could happen next.
Then someone arrived and said, “The men you put in prison are in the temple, standing there and teaching the people.”
The captain went with the officers and brought the apostles in—but without using force. They were afraid the people might stone them.
They brought the apostles before the council, and the high priest questioned them.
“Didn’t we strictly order you not to teach in this name? Yet look—you’ve filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you’re trying to make us responsible for this man’s death.”
Peter and the other apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than people.
The God of our ancestors raised Jesus, the one you killed by hanging him on a tree.
God lifted him up to his right hand as Leader and Savior, so Israel could turn back to God and have their sins forgiven.
We are witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.”
When they heard this, the council members were furious and wanted to kill the apostles.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up. He was a respected teacher of the Law, honored by all the people. He ordered the apostles taken outside for a little while.
Then he said, “People of Israel, think carefully about what you’re about to do to these men.
Some time ago, Theudas showed up claiming to be somebody important. About four hundred men joined him. He was killed, his followers scattered, and his movement came to nothing.
After him, Judas the Galilean came along during the census and drew people after him. He too was killed, and all his followers scattered.
So here’s my advice: leave these men alone. If this plan or work is only human, it will collapse.
But if it comes from God, you won’t be able to stop it. You may even end up fighting God.”
They agreed with him. They called the apostles back in, had them beaten, ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
The apostles left the council, glad they had been counted worthy to suffer shame for the name of Jesus.
Every day, in the temple and in people’s homes, they kept teaching and announcing the good news that Jesus is the Messiah.
